notes:
T427 (does the argus-doctor regression stop leaking fixture rows into the live kanban?) — answered yes, with the mechanism fixed and the detection added. T425 delivered `argus --mode doctor` and its regression wrote 16 T425-DOCTOR-* rows into the LIVE kanban (13.5% of the store; removed by the Orchestrator on 2026-08-08 after bundle-path verification). This row fixes the cause in three places, all test-first.

WHAT THE INCIDENT WAS: tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh arms 2 and 7 called `managent add/claim/done` without MANAGENT_STORE, so the controls wrote to the default store — the live docs/infra/managent/tasks.json. Reproduced on a COPY of the live store (the brief's seeded control): the pre-fix script added 2 T425-DOCTOR-2/7-<rand> rows to whatever store managent was pointed at, proving the write mechanism that polluted live 16 times. Nothing detected it — not claimlint, not the suite, not `managent audit`.

FIX 1 — the regression (tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh): every managent call — the test's writes AND the doctor's internal `bin/managent status --json`/`liveness` — now runs against a SCRATCH kanban store seeded with a byte-copy of the live store (MANAGENT_STORE exported for the whole script). The script ends with the deliverable null control (arm 15): live tasks.json byte-identical before and after the full run (sha256 compared; 15 other arms run in between, including two that plant kanban rows and one that runs the doctor against the live store).

FIX 2 — the mechanism (src/managent/main.zig, rebuilt + deployed): the brief offered three options (fixture-pattern refusal on live add; test-harness-marker refusal of live writes; argus refusing mutating verbs) and asked for the one that fails loudly at the moment of the write. Chosen: BOTH managent guards, because the leak is a kanban-store write and that is where 'the moment of the write' lives. (1) `add` of a row whose id contains a boundary-delimited fixture marker (DOCTOR/FIXTURE/SEED/PROBE/ARM/TEST) is REFUSED on the live store with exit 1 — no cooperation required from the caller, the id itself trips it, so the T425 shape cannot recur even from a harness that forgets every env var. (2) MANAGENT_TEST=1 refuses ALL mutating verbs (add/claim/done/reopen/purge/set/needs/agent/verdict/archive/amend/sync/tell/inbox/dispatch/suggest/next/ping, plus the load-time migration write) on the live store — a self-declared harness cannot write production even with a non-fixture-shaped id. 'Live store' is MANAGENT_STORE unset OR resolving (symlinks included) to the default path — the /tmp→/private/tmp macOS symlink was a real bug found by the test (case b of arm 12 wrote a row before realpath was added). Scratch stores are exempt: tests own their substrate. Option 3 (argus refuses mutating verbs) is implemented as a cheap belt in bin/argus (a _managent() helper with a read-only verb allowlist that raises on any mutating verb) but is explicitly NOT the primary guard — the T425 leak came from the regression calling managent directly, not from argus, so guarding argus alone would not have prevented it.

FIX 3 — the detection (bin/argus --mode doctor, 10th check): a row is flagged under NEEDS ACTION when its id matches the fixture pattern OR (bundle under tools//bin/ AND claimed==done to the second). claimed==done alone is deliberately NOT a signal — 6 legit live rows (T380/T400/T349/T388/T367/T371) close within the same second, and the detector must not false-alarm on them; the incident rows had all three signals. The doctor reads the kanban store directly (honoring MANAGENT_STORE) because `managent status --json` omits claimed/done timestamps.

CONTROLS — test-first, 16 arms in tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh (wired into zig build test): 0-10 the T425 arms (arms 2/7 re-pointed at the scratch store; their planted rows are deleted from scratch, not closed, so arm 11's clean assertion cannot trip on a -DOCTOR- id); 11 seeded (plant one fixture-shaped row in the SCRATCH store — the exact incident shape — doctor reports it under NEEDS ACTION; after removal the report is clean); 12 seeded (managent REFUSES fixture-pattern add on the live store in a FAKE repo, both MANAGENT_STORE-unset and set-to-default-path; the same add on a scratch store succeeds — the 'unless MANAGENT_STORE is set' semantics; the fake repo keeps the guard test zero-risk against the real live store); 13 seeded (MANAGENT_TEST=1 refuses a mutating verb on the live store, read-only verbs keep working, scratch stays allowed); 14 null (doctor against the REAL live store reports zero fixture rows — the 16 are gone, no false alarm); 15 null (live tasks.json byte-identical after the whole run). RED on the pre-fix code: arms 11-14 failed (no detection, add succeeded on the live store — fake_gained=1, MANAGENT_TEST ignored), arm 15 passed because the new script already isolates. GREEN on the post-fix code: 16/16 PASS, live tasks.json byte-identical, git tree clean afterwards. The deployed bin/managent was rebuilt (zig build) and deployed (zig build deploy) so the regression exercises the guard; arm 6 (deploy staleness) confirmed the full deploy restored 'zero stale'.

BARS:
- tools/regression-argus-doctor.sh, bin/argus, findings file — delivered. The 16 removed rows were NOT re-added (arm 14 confirms zero fixture rows on the real store).
- argus read-only by contract: R3 write allowlist unchanged (three paths); R5 one mode per invocation unchanged; the new _managent() helper enforces the read-only verb allowlist (option 3, kept as a belt).
- Every figure with its denominator.
- Findings file conforming (bin/weizigo-claimlint: C7 non-conforming 0).

OTHER-LEAK SWEEP (brief item 4): the live store was swept for rows whose bundle does not exist or points outside untracked/ and docs/infra/dispatch/. Denominator 105 rows, 104 with a bundle: 0 missing bundles (0/104); 0 bundles outside the two allowed directories (0/104; STANDING-ABSORB and STANDING-CLEANUP use absolute paths that resolve inside docs/infra/dispatch/ and are counted allowed). The store carries no other leak of the T425 shape.

IMPLICATION FOR T426 (assertion-ledger spec): this incident is the worked example its anti-skip section demands — the write happened, nothing refused it, and no gap was visible afterwards (the third category its spec says must not exist). The fix demonstrates the shape of the third category's cure: refuse at the write (managent guards), detect at the surface (doctor check 10), and prove byte-identity at the harness boundary (arm 15).

DEPLOYMENT: bin/managent rebuilt and deployed; bin/argus is a Python script shipped at HEAD (no build step). zig build deploy ran to restore bin/==zig-out (arm 6).

LANDMARK: advances L4 (the ledger is clean) — the live kanban can no longer be written by a test harness (two managent guards refuse at the moment of the write), the regression that leaked is now substrate-isolated with a byte-identical proof, and the watchdog that failed to notice sixteen fake consoles in its own input now reports the next one under NEEDS ACTION on its weekly sweep.
